SEND Provision
SEND Provision at Kingswood House
Introduction
As a mainstream school, Kingswood House is unique in that it is so inclusive and, also, in the depth and breadth or support we can provide. Our small class sizes make a huge difference – we have a maximum of eighteen students in class, often fewer. The school site is relatively compact – so it’s not intimidating and there is less sensory overload and with only 230 students in the whole school no pupil is ever ‘anonymous’ or ‘overlooked’ at Kingswood House.
Our ambition is always to support our pupils with learning difficulties to be able to fully realise their true potential. The simple reality is that many of these pupils have strengths in areas traditional testing and education just doesn’t value and often they’ll find the conventional education approach a challenge.
At Kingswood House we pride ourselves on being able to provide an individualised supportive system more tailored to our pupils’ needs.
Becky Lawrence Head of SEND
Our Approach to SEND
Here at Kingswood House we Believe having great Special Educational Needs and Disabilities provision is not just important – it is essential. It reflects the school’s commitment to inclusivity, equality, and the belief that every child, regardless of their individual challenges, has the right to the highest-quality education and boundless opportunity to thrive.
Children with SEND often face barriers to learning that others do not, whether these are related to cognition, communication, social-emotional development, or physical needs. Without the right support, these barriers can lead to a lack of confidence, low achievement, and disengagement from learning. Here we can offer tailored interventions, compassionate teaching, and a strong support system, which means pupils with SEND can flourish both academically and personally.
Excellent SEND provision ensures that pupils’ needs are identified early, supported effectively, and that they are empowered to reach their full potential. This might include one-to-one support, differentiated teaching strategies, specialist interventions, assistive technology, or simply a nurturing environment that allows them to feel safe, valued, and understood.
Our SEND provision is personalised and individualised; all the staff know the students and adapt, if a pupil needs extra support, we have speech and language therapists, occupational therapists, dyslexia tutors and specialist maths tutors. Fifty-three percent of the school access this extra provision, it is not unusual, seeking support and asking for help is part of life at KHS.
We Believe great SEND provision is not just about helping pupils cope – it’s about helping them excel. It shifts the narrative from “disability” to “possibility”, encouraging students to embrace their strengths and build self-belief. This kind of provision promotes resilience, independence, and a lifelong love of learning. Importantly, it also benefits the whole school community by fostering empathy, patience, and a culture of respect.
For families, knowing their child is in a school that understands and supports their needs brings reassurance and partnership. It builds trust and opens communication between school and home – essential elements for any child’s success.
Ultimately, we hope the strength of our SEND provision reflects our values as a school and our dedication to every learner. We Believe part of our job is to prepare all our pupils – not just those with SEND – to live in a diverse society where everyone has something valuable to contribute. Inclusive education isn’t just about supporting some – it’s about enriching the experience for all.
Becky Lawrence Head of SEND
Muddy Stilettos Best Learning Support – Finalist
We are absolutely delighted to announce that Kingswood House School has been named a FINALIST in the Muddy Stilettos Best Schools Awards 2025 in the category of Best Learning Support!
“From the boy who honestly could barely catch a ball and who would hide in assemblies, to A Teams sports and cricket captain, top scores in assessments and speaking in front of large groups, we can scarcely believe the transformation.”
“I think Kingswood House works really hard to get to know each child individually and celebrate who they are - they create an environment where everyone feels accepted and comfortable.”
“Kingswood House is the missing piece of the puzzle in a lot of kids’ educational journeys. There are not many schools quite like it. When you find it, and you’ve been looking for it for some time, and your child suddenly blossoms, it’s magical.”
“The school is great at seeing the child for who they are as an individual with their own personality and any problems they may have and working with them to develop them into confident young adults.”
“While it will never be the first choice of parents motivated principally by stellar academic results or dinner party bragging rights, it has carved out a niche as a truly inclusive school where pupils, often crushed by previous educational experiences, can blossom, start to love school and do well.”
“I think the pupils here are each in their own lane, all the children here are in their own lane …and they just happily run alongside each other”
The Study Centre
Our Study Centre has been an integral part of KHS since 1989. It was created to meet the needs of pupils with mild to moderate dyslexia, ASD and ADHD and shows our commitment to being a truly inclusive mainstream school offering an outstanding, all-round education from age 7 (Year 3) up to age 16 (Year 11).
A wide range of specialist teaching and learning professionals work within our Study Centre to oversee the best possible support provision for pupils with SEND. Our fully integrated team work closely with classroom staff and parents to provide expert 1:1 and small-group tuition.

“Parents spoke highly of the bespoke nature of the learning experience for their children at the school and the successes their children have experienced. They evidenced the significant level of communication and interaction in support of their child to make excellent all-round progress, both in and out of the classroom. They further commented on the care and thought by teachers and the positive relationship in communication with their children observed during home schooling”
Emotional Literacy Support
Parents choose us because they appreciate that strong pastoral care, individual attention to pupil details and smaller class sizes offer the foundation for each child to flourish. The role of an ELSA in school offers an additional pastoral layer which demonstrates how our pupils’ well-being and mental health is a major, collective priority for us all.
Our ELSA is Ms Katey Timothy, a specialist with a wealth of experience of working with children. ELSAs are trained and regularly supervised by the Educational Psychologists in the local education authority. An ELSA aims to remove the barriers to learning and to have happy children in school and at home; in the first instance, referrals to Ms Timothy are made via the form teacher but she is directly contactable by the pupils as well.
Download our Emotional Literacy Introduction and our ELSA leaflet here:
Gifted, Talented & Interested
Nurturing talent and passions
At Kingswood House, pupils may be identified as gifted, talented or interested (GTi) in a subject.
“Every day the word 'gift' is used to define talent, ability, and performance. Being gifted has an even deeper meaning, a meaning that isn't always measured in points per game, wins or loses - it's measured by heart, effort, and desire.”
What does being ‘gifted, talented and interested’ mean?
Simply put, pupils who show exceptional aptitude and/or interest within a subject. The identification of a GTi pupil will utilise evidence from a variety of sources:
Attainment in class
What happens when my child is identified as ‘gifted’, ‘talented’ or ‘interested’ (GTi) in a subject?
Work will be carefully differentiated to ensure that your son or daughter is receiving an appropriate level of support and challenge. Pupils are also encouraged to take part in extra-curricular projects and events within school as well as engage with extra-curricular opportunities. Gifted, talented and interested projects run alongside Kingswood House’s subject enrichment program, taking inspiration from national initiatives such as British Science week. Because talent can be evidenced at any time during a child’s development, teachers may identify pupils at any time throughout their schooling.

Careers
Careers
Careers at Kingswood House
The world of work has changed beyond recognition in the 21st century, and even since the pandemic. At KHS we pride ourselves on giving children’s futures, and careers, top priority. This means an enlightened, progressive and personalised approach, extending far beyond the reach of simple academic grades. The Careers programme at KHS, therefore, aims to inspire students to develop the confidence, knowledge and human skills which will support their individual ambitions in the future.
The Careers programme encompasses work experience as well as guidance on 16+ destinations. In both respects, there is no ‘one size fits all’ at a school which welcomes such a diverse pupil body. Just as KHS students leave us to go to academic independent schools, local sixth form colleges, specialist performing arts settings, boarding schools and everything in between, so too we envisage our students setting their sights on careers in every industry from the traditional city offices to creatives to entrepreneurship. KHS students are exactly the kind of open-minded thinkers who will take on those roles which don’t even exist yet – maybe underwater farmers or avatar relationship managers?
Guided by the Gatsby benchmarks, specific guidance and advice is offered at every stage. This ranges from workshops and events to guest speakers and access to the Morrisby platform. Students receive individual Careers appointments and specific interview and CV writing practice. A wide range of extra-curricular clubs and activities outside the classroom allows every student the opportunity to explore and develop areas of special interest.
From the individualised pastoral care and support, through to your child’s group participation as part of the House system, the whole KHS journey ensures the development of every child’s individual identity and sense of self, which will ultimately make the difference to their academic and professional future.

Extra Curricular Clubs & Activities
Introduction
At Kingswood House, we are guided by the premise that children who are secure, active and happy in their learning will develop the self-belief and independence that lead to academic success and a sense of fulfilment.
We are proud of our reputation for being a nurturing school which recognises the individual needs and strengths of each of its pupils. Alongside exceptional pastoral care and excellent teaching, we offer a range of extracurricular clubs and activities that is broad, balanced and engaging.
We firmly believe that learning takes place as much outside of the classroom as it does inside – so our pupils are warmly encouraged to undertake one or two clubs or activities per week in order to help them acquire new skills, foster collaborative teamwork, and, of course, to have enormous fun into the bargain.
Clubs & Activities
We always do our best to cater to any interests expressed by our students and new clubs and activities are therefore added on a regular basis.

Activities on site include a wide range of sport and games sessions, art and crafts practical fun, use of our ICT suite and much more! There are also optional excursions to local venues, driven in our minibuses, which can be booked as part of your day at an extra cost.

Staff & Governors
Senior Leadership Team
Matthew Bryan
MA (Cantab.), MA (Oxon.), MSC, PGCE, FRSA
Matthew joined KHS in April 2024, having spent six years as Head at Longacre prep school in Surrey. Before that his career took him from London day schools in Hampton and Wimbledon to boarding prep in Oxfordshire and Kent. His journey from traditional to progressive, from single-sex to co-ed, from 1000+ students to individual attention, led him to the firm belief that Kingswood House represents not just an invaluable educational option for families in this area, but also an exemplar of what a dynamic, pupil-centred, values-led 21st century can look like.
In spite of wanting to break the mould and run a different kind of school to the more stereotypical independent Surrey offering, Matthew feels very lucky to be married with two teenage children, a black Labrador and a poorly-trained Cavapoo. During his free time he enjoys yoga, talking about educational theory and riding carbon-fibre bikes which were designed for cyclists lighter and faster than he.
Liam Clarke
Kingswood House has been a significant part of my life for nearly forty years. As an ex-pupil, current parent and a teacher here for the last 21 years, I feel I speak with considerable insight when I say there is simply nowhere better in bringing out the best in every single pupil. I am passionate about education but it has to be about the child and enabling pupils to achieve in a caring, nurturing environment – that is Kingswood House, which is why I have found it impossible to leave the school. My long term dream came true earlier in the year when I was Interim Head for two terms; a role in which I took great pride. I am now Deputy Head and am loving the challenge of this role; importantly it means I spend more time with pupils which is vital to me.
Family is important to me. I have 5 children, one of whom attends Kingswood House. My wife and I have bought our dream home and enjoy time developing parts of the house and garden in our spare time. I am a member at Tyrells Wood Golf Club and enjoy a round of golf with friends when I get the chance. I also have a season ticket at Chelsea Football club and often go with family and friends.
Jamie Green
BA (Hons) Marketing Communications, PGCE, MA International Education, TESOL, QTS
Ever since I helped my old primary school during university holidays, I’ve been involved in education. I spent seven fantastic years in Hong Kong where I worked for an educational charity before training as a teacher and obtaining both my PGCE and Masters in International Education from Sunderland University. When not studying, I spent my time hiking the mountains or playing football at the prestigious Hong Kong Football Club, where I made some of my best memories.
In 2020, I returned to the UK with my wife and worked my way up the management of Falcons School in Putney. My teaching philosophy recognises the role of wellbeing in achieving academic progress, and I always aim to bring positivity into the classroom. The inclusive, wholesome nature of Kingswood House School is what drew me in, and something I am very excited to be a part of.
Sachin Sukhdeo
BSc (Hons) Maths, Dip. Secondary Education, QTS
Born in South Africa, I pursued my passion for sports and education, training as a teacher at the University of Natal. I further developed my qualifications with a Bachelor of Science from the Open University and Qualified Teacher Status from the University of Buckingham. My career commenced in Johannesburg, teaching secondary mathematics and physical education. Seeking new experiences, I relocated to the UK, taking on teaching roles in London across both state and independent schools. I’ve acquired extensive experience and held numerous middle management and senior leadership positions, culminating in my current role as Head of Seniors.
I have a keen interest in neurodiversity, artificial intelligence in education, and sports and firmly believe education is the most formidable instrument for changing the world. Working at Kingswood House, I am continually awestruck by our students’ incredible journeys and progression. I take pride in fostering a nurturing, supportive environment where pupils feel valued, respected, and empowered to explore their interests and abilities without fear of judgment – a catalyst for self-confidence.
Beyond the classroom, you’ll find me on the tennis court indulging my love for the sport or at the gym. Weekends, I proudly embrace the role of a football and netball dad, cheering on my kids, and spending quality time in the kitchen, cooking up culinary delights!
Becky Lawrence
B.A. (Hons) History, P.G.C.E., Q.T.S., C.P.T.3A., B. Ed. (SEND)
I have been working in education now for over fifteen years, for the last four years as a SENDCo.
As a SENDCo I believe passionately in inclusive teaching and equality. I find it enormously fulfilling helping a student discover the way they personally learn best, understanding their needs and working with them to establish the most effective ways to support them as an individual. I believe in praise and the ‘Power of Yes’ …always encouraging a positive mindset.
Joining Kingswood this year as the SENDCo is an exciting new chapter and I look forward to becoming an integral part of the school community.
I originally trained as a history teacher and I am still hugely engaged by that world and enjoy visiting historical sites, travelling and culture. I also am a bibliophile and can often be found reading another book when I am not out walking my dog, Toby.
Julia Hodgkins
BEd Hons PE & RS, MA (Guidance & Counselling), Minst F (Cert)
I was drawn to Kingswood House by the differences it offers. An inspiring educational ethos, and a deep commitment to offering every pupil an opportunity to achieve their best, within a warm and nurturing environment. I have worked in education for over 35 years both as a teacher, senior manager and as Head of Development, raising money for bursaries and capital projects in both the state and independent sector, single-sex and co-ed schools, Prep and Secondary.
At the core of Development and Fundraising is relationship building and I am looking forward to getting to know the parents and families here at Kingswood House and helping to strengthen and build our community, past and present.
Akila Garrib
Kathy Bees
ACMA, CGMA, BComm (Hons) Business Management, BComms Business Studies
I moved to England at 23 after earning an Honours in Business Management and pursued a postgraduate path, qualifying as a Chartered Management Accountant (CIMA). I began my career in the high-end corporate hospitality sector, working with Mark Birley’s Association and Home House, where I gained deep experience in hospitality operations and management accounting, gradually shifting into broader strategic finance roles.
After the birth of my daughter, I felt compelled to change direction and trained as a multi-sport coach, launching a kids’ sports coaching business for ages 18 months to 7 years. This venture ignited my interest in education, leveraging sports and game-based activities to support learning and fundamental movement skills outside a traditional school setting.
In 2019, due to personal circumstances, I closed the business and joined White Spider Climbing as Finance Manager, contributing beyond standard accounting to operational strategy as part of the management team.
I accepted the role of Bursar at Kingswood House School to align my professional skills with my passion for children’s education, within a traditional school environment that remains non-stereotypical for independent schools.
I’m an avid runner (when not injured), active lifestyle enthusiast, and climber – even fortunate enough to have taken part in the Paris Olympic Marathon Pour Tour in August 2024. I play cricket for Epsom Cricket Club Women’s Team, assist with coaching and love paddle boarding.
Department Heads
Luke Allen
This is my second year at Kingswood House School. Prior to this I had a varied career in teaching spanning nearly 30 years. After graduating from University with a Bachelor of Music degree I started teaching in Hampshire, staying in the area for ten years, having time in both secondary and primary schools, always as Director of Music. I then spent another few years in FE back in my native Somerset, lecturing up to degree level. I then upped-sticks and moved to Suffolk, experiencing the independent sector for the first time, culminating in taking the role of Bandmaster at Royal Hospital School, providing the students with varied opportunities from training at the Royal Marines School of Music, to them performing at the Royal Variety Performance in the middle of lockdown!
I passionately believe that music education should be for all, irrespective or opportunities they have had before. My lessons are built around enthusiasm, encouragement and giving-it-a-go. This is what makes Kingswood House such a special place to be, the joy the students get from seeing their peers perform, and the realisation that they can do it too, is unique in a place like this. This feeling is then taken in to other aspects of school life, giving all students the confidence that they can succeed.
Rudi Anthony
BA Accounting & Finance, PGCE
Prior to becoming a teacher Rudi served in the British Army. Rudi has implemented student-driven projects, and developed schoolwide computer science and STEM integration units that emphasise the metacognition and learning process through computer science concepts and computational thinking practices. In addition to developing the school’s Computer Science Framework, he has been involved in drafting the Digital Learning Strategy for the school. Rudi promotes the integration of computer science as an essential part of academic learning and of digital literacy development. Rudi is committed to expanding computer science education in KHS and is dedicated to supporting the digital learning and development of inspired and innovative educators.
Christopher Belcher
BSc (Exercise & Sports Science) PGCE
I have been teaching for 9 years across 3 schools and have taught a wide range of subjects, from PE, Science, Health, Catering and Design Technology, and am now here as the Head of Design Technology.
Prior to joining KHS I have worked in two large state schools in Isleworth and Staines, which feel like a totally different world! I have only been here since January but already feel very welcomed by both staff and students.
I am keen to be able to spend time with students to provide them with the opportunity and resources to develop as independent learners. KHS is a fantastic environment to be able to do this, with smaller classes and support available to students right the way through the school.
Providing students with a space to be able to ask questions and build their knowledge in a safe space will help students to be more confident in their abilities, both practical and theoretical.
James Earl-King
BSc (Hons) PCE Primary Education
I have been involved in sport since Primary School as a competitor in a plethora of sports and began my paradigm shift to coaching in my early twenties. Having garnered eighteen years of experience at all levels and age groups as a coach, as a teacher, Head of external coaching programmes and further as a Head of Department at Tormead School, following a short career break where I explored other career interests, I returned to education.
I have continued to improve and refine my approach to delivering sport through personal methodologies and philosophies that are the root of my reason for being involved in these disciplines: I believe that anyone can achieve their potential if they want it enough; that sport is a metaphor for life; that a team is only as strong as its weakest member – so it’s the teams’ responsibility to strengthen that player; and that the value of the team is greater than the sum of its parts.
PE and sports play such an important role in that they can add value to all aspects of education and intersect with all academic subjects. I see Kingswood House as a place where the philosophies of the school closely align with my own, and I see the school as an environment that looks far beyond the academic attainment of an individual to enable them to develop their innate qualities in a diverse range of ways: focusing on helping individuals achieving their greatest potential.
Julie Haunstetter
B.A. (Hons) Medieval and Modern History, P.G.C.E
My job prior to teaching was in banking, something which I enjoyed for 15 years. I then had a career break whilst my three children were young, though during this time I was closely involved with their primary school in Wimbledon as a volunteer and as a governor. This, combined with my passion for History, led me to retrain and become a teacher.
My first teaching role was at Carshalton Boys’ Sports College, where I was a Head of Year. I then moved for a short time to Ursuline High School in Wimbledon as Head of Department.
Having spent 4 years at Kingswood House my enthusiasm for my subject and for helping young people to develop remains as strong as ever. Each child we teach deserves to flourish and be supported in all that they do so that they can attain their very best, and I whole-heartedly believe that we enable and encourage every single student at KHS the opportunity to do just that.
Outside of school, I continue to be a history-geek, often attending talks and lectures, as well as the odd spot of mud-larking along the Thames! I love running, walking, going to the theatre with my friends and family and travelling as far and as wide as possible.
Thomas Laudy

Sport for All
Our goal is to make sport at Kingswood House accessible to every student through a wide range of co-curricular activities, competitive fixtures, and House Sport events.
Providing opportunities for pupils to participate in different activities is at the heart of Sport at Kingswood House. We provide a wide range of sports for our pupils, catering to both those who relish competition as well as those who just want to have fun and stay fit. The aim of the sports department is to instil an understanding of the importance of physical activity and help pupils learn the key benefits of sport.
We aim to offer everyone the chance to represent the school in a variety of sports and competitive matches each term, ranging from elite performers at national level to those who prefer their sport to be more recreational. We often compete against much bigger schools with a great deal of success and we adapt our fixture programme to ensure that matches are as competitive as possible.
Our sport and coaching programmes focus on core fitness principles such as agility, cardio-vascular endurance and coordination as well as building wide-ranging sports familiarity and encouraging our pupils to try out different team-based and individual sports and recreational opportunities.
Pupils throughout the school have two whole afternoons of sport each week, equating to around four hours of coaching/playing time.

Senior School
“I’m committed to nurturing our students’ development, helping them thrive both academically and in their overall well-being.”
Introduction
Thanks for coming through to this part about our Senior School. It’s just a short overview of what we do – and what we don’t do!
KHS gives senior students the best parts of Prep school, adjusted to be appropriate for young people in the 21st century. This means continuing with small class sizes, having sensible amounts of homework, a balanced day with plenty of outdoor time and teachers who are kind and helpful, and who know you as an individual.
We don’t believe in a 11+ test, nor in regular and stressful class tests. Your teachers will monitor your progress and give you feedback on how you’re doing, and how they think you can improve. Your voice really matters, and there are many ways to (politely, of course!) make comments on the options you’re given, the balance of freedom versus support, whether the tasks you’re doing are giving you the chance to show your potential.
We have residential trips for Years 7 and 8, and then there are subject-specific trips for Years 9-11 to support your subject options. Year 11s carry the most senior roles in the school – until they have other things to focus on in the summer and the Year 10s take over. The oldest children take on Mentor roles to look after the Year 7s, ensuring that there is a positive cycle of helping and reassuring those less experienced than ourselves.
Students in the Senior school choose bespoke pathways. That means an array of options in traditional and less traditional subjects for GCSE, Cambridge National and BTEC qualifications. It means being able to get involved in DofE, or HPQ. It means all kinds of creative outlets. It means being prepared for highly academic 6th forms, or more hands-on apprenticeships and everything in between. It means being treated with respect as you approach adulthood, while never leaving you to fend for yourself.

Our Approach to Homework
Our new approach to homework at KHS
At Kingswood House we Believe nothing tells you more about a school’s culture, how it balances traditional wisdom with modern research, how it seeks to help its pupils to get the best learning over a sustained period of time, and how it understands the whole life of a child and a family, not just the narrow parts we see in the school day, than the school’s approach to homework.
Poorly handled, homework is too often a source of anxiety for young people. Too often the catalyst for battles at home. Too often irrelevant, or inaccessible, or boring. Any of these will almost certainly prevent a learner from learning, rendering the whole process stressful and pointless.
So why have homework at all? Because done right, it can be powerful for cementing understanding, developing independence, sparking excitement and allowing children to delve deep into the fascinating and inspiring cultural capital that we call our curriculum.
Have a quick search online and you’ll find an avalanche of academic research, trying to understand why ‘how’ homework is done is so much more meaningful than ‘how much’. For a child’s-eye view, check out Mikel Garmendia’s eloquent TED talk.
Here at Kingswood, we are endlessly passionate about children being happy, about giving them the best platform to achieve their potential, about having the best possible understanding between teachers, parents and students.
That’s why we take homework seriously.
Key Stage 3 & 4 Homework explained
To find out more about our new approach to homework, what’s changing and how, please click the link below.
Senior Options
Senior options and pathways explained
Kingswood House is all about giving you, the student, the best opportunities to show what you’re capable of, to develop your skills, and to build a platform to give yourself every chance to achieve your dreams.
It’s about giving you support where you need it, so that you can get better at things which are important, but tricky, as well as allowing you to lean into your strengths and your passions.
What this means in practice is that there is a huge range and flexibility when it comes to making your options.
Firstly, whatever you choose will start at the beginning of Year 9. That gives our students three years to cover the syllabus, practise techniques and gain a really full understanding of a subject before sitting their exams.
Secondly, there is no ‘one size fits all’ approach to which subjects you do, or how many. Most of our students will take 8 or 9 subjects. There are different approaches available for English, and different levels for Maths and Science. Some students take foreign languages, but not all. Subjects are offered as GCSEs, iGCSEs, BTECs and Cambridge Nationals.
Each year, the number of options available grows, and we want KHS students to select a bespoke portfolio of subjects, whether theoretical, practical or a mixture, which suits them. That large number of options means that classes are often very small indeed – mostly in single figures – allowing students to have maximum 1:1 time with their teachers.
Aside from the subjects that you choose, there’s a number of ways in which your experience in these crucial years is rounded out and made relevant for modern life. Whether that means HPQ, or gaining a Duke of Edinburgh award, or pursuing a number of work experience options, or simply learning to get the most out of ‘town leave’ time in Epsom, we never forget that education is about much more than lesson time.
I hope you enjoy reading this brochure, and that you find some options here which get you excited about starting the next phase of your journey at Kingswood House.

Trips & Residentials
At Kingswood House School, we believe in holistic, practical, experience-based learning for pupils as individuals and in groups. Residential trips are a crucial way to learn and grow outside the classroom, offering opportunity, inclusivity and familiarity. Trips are the perfect chance for pupils to step out of their comfort zone, make new friends, and increase rapport and confidence with classmates and teachers. These residential trips perfectly complement the wide array of academic and pastorally relevant day trips through the school year.
Residential trips enable our pupils to pick up important life skills. Whether it’s working as a team, taking the lead, or solving problems, these experiences are invaluable. Being out in nature, out of the ‘bubble’ of school, brings learning to life and shapes memories that last forever.
Our trip program at Kingswood House is all about enriching both children’s learning and life experiences. We look for all pupils in Years 3 – 8 to participate in our trips. For younger children, this is often their first time away from home and we understand how much confidence and support is sometimes needed (that goes for parents just as much as pupils!). It is vital that these experiences are positive, and set children up to succeed. In Years 9 and upwards, there is a range of trips directly linked to various GCSE and BTEC subjects. In the spirit of inclusivity, however, we look to make trips open to all students, rather than only those doing a certain subject.

About Us
Our School
Our Ethos
When looking at schools, many people are tempted to compare facilities, or exam results, or gender ratios, or any other easily quantifiable metric. In reality though, it is more often the intangibles, the hard to pin down more elusive qualities like values, culture, character and spirit that really set one school apart from another. We believe it is these qualities that determine the single most important aspect of how a school operates, that shape and define a pupil’s experience at school, and that should be the basis on which a parent should choose a school for their child.
Both children and adults at KHS will use lots of words to describe Kingswood House. But one word rises above all others: believe. Our belief system is to believe in children. We know it works, because to believe is to have hope, and to have hope is the key to being happy.
And that happiness is at the centre of every decision we make. It’s why we have such small class sizes. It’s why the school has a strict limit of 275 pupils – once you go much higher than that, you can no longer promise that every adult will know every child. It’s why we have a ‘cab rank’ approach to admissions and don’t have an 11+ exam, or any other academic barriers to entry. If we can offer an education to a child, and we have an available space, then that’s all there is to it.
The provision looks different whether you’re 7 or 16, whether you’re indoors or outdoors, at work or play. But the ethos stays the same: we believe in the power of education to transform a child’s life and prospects; pupils learn to believe that they can make a difference, no matter what their own unique blend of strengths and difficulties; we believe teachers who care make the biggest impact.
At the end of the day, though, these are just words. My promise to you is that you’ll feel the ethos at Kingswood House if you come to visit us. It’s a special place, and I’ll look forward to living up to the big promises I’ve made above. If you want to see a school which thinks a bit differently, please do submit an enquiry online, or give our Head of Admissions, Ellie Barrett, a ring. I’ll look forward to meeting you.
In the meantime, if you’d like to get an initial feel for our ethos press play to hear what our pupils and staff have to say about our school.

Our Core Values
Co-Education
Kingswood House went co-ed in 2021: the school might be 125 years old, but we are always looking for ways to improve the school and give pupils bigger and better opportunities. Expanding the school to include girls was the biggest example of this, and the positive impact of having girls here has been just as huge.
Life is co-ed. School is about learning the vital skills and knowledge that you will need throughout your adult life. That means learning about yourself, as well as about other people. We have girls working with boys, as well as artists working with scientists, sporty types and musicians, children who have a range of interests and those who haven’t found their ‘thing’ yet. The broad mix of both pupils and staff at KHS ensures that we have varied perspectives and holistic development for all.
Every single area of school life has improved as a result of the move to co-education, and after only this short space of time it is already impossible to imagine life without girls! The success is down to the fact that nothing is taken for granted. Everyone in our school community works to ensure that all children are happy, have what they need, and share in the responsibility to keep improving.
Kingswood House is committed to nurturing pupils in an inclusive, safe, respectful and diverse environment. This is the best – the only – way to prepare them for the complexities, challenges and opportunities of adult life.
Pastoral Care and Well-being
Pastoral care. Keeping children safe. Strong role modelling. Focusing on your mental health and wellbeing. Important words, and words which are at the very heart of our life and our values at Kingswood House. But just words, and they’re quite similar to the words you see promised at every school. So here’s the part where we try to explain why we’re different, why so many children feel a different experience at Kingswood House compared to their last school, and why pastoral care will always be something that defines our school.
At Kingswood House, our motto is ‘believe’. Belief underpins everything we do. When it comes to pastoral care, we believe that what children say is important, and needs to be listened to. Student voice is central to big decisions. When children feel listened to, and valued, they are more likely to be confident and more likely to tell adults what they’re experiencing.
We have small classes, so your form teacher will know you really well. We have Katey, our ELSA, who’s always on hand, or Emma our nurse. Or Karen and Anne in the office. The teachers all know all the pupils, and they always have time to listen. Sometimes, pupils feel the person they want to talk to is an LSA from the Study Centre. Then we have a lot of staff meetings so we can share what we know as adults, and ensure that children get the support they need.
Sometimes pastoral care is about believing in your potential, and not letting you fall short of your capabilities. Pastoral care means talking with pupils about how classes are going, whether homework is manageable, are pupils doing enough – or too many?! – clubs and activities. It means grown ups showing the respect, tolerance and kindness which we ask for from our children, and holding pupils accountable for their actions. Life is not about avoiding mistakes – mistakes are inevitable. What matters is how you learn from them and make improvements.
The pastoral care system at Kingswood House is about communication, respect, belief, kindness and setting ourselves high standards. Safety and tolerance are essential, and these things can only exist when everyone in a community believes in them, and lives them on a daily basis. Hopefully you believe in these things too.
Diversity, Equality and Inclusion
Kingswood House is a fully inclusive school, you can see and feel it from the moment you walk through our doors, and we firmly believe that everyone within our school community should feel safe, respected, secure and valued.
For us, promoting equal opportunities is fundamental to the aims and ethos of our school, as are the benefits of having a diverse school community, with individuals who value one another and the different contributions each individual can make and who treat each other with kindness, thoughtfulness and respect.
Within the school, pupils experience an environment where daily they are immersed in a culture that encourages, models and celebrates what it means to value and respect others.
We are committed to being an equal opportunities school and to equal treatment for all pupils, and staff, regardless of race, sex, disability, religion or belief, sexual orientation, gender reassignment, marital status, pregnancy or maternity (the “protected characteristics”).

Prep School Prospectus
Let’s talk about our Prep school – a whistlestop tour of some of the nuts and bolts of prep life.
Here we have the ideal balance: first and foremost is your Form teacher who you see every day, who teaches you key subjects and knows all of their 15 (or so) pupils inside out and back to front. Then there are subject specialist teachers allowing pupils to get expert guidance in subjects like Art and PE where the depth of their professional knowledge really helps to prepare young people and give them the best foundations in that subject.
At the beginning of the prep journey, homework must focus only on reading at home, along with fundamental fluencies of mathematics such as number bonds or times tables. High frequency word spellings would be added to this as appropriate. That’s enough, no need for complex science investigations or scale models of Tudor houses (which, let’s face it, are usually homework tasks for parents anyway).
Older prep pupils will develop these tasks into a little more writing, thinking and learning. But never more than 30 minutes work, and many pupils will take advantage of the chance to do ‘homework’ at school before they leave, meaning that when they do get home, they’re done for the day. Leaving room for some bedtime reading, perhaps.
The oldest children in Prep will be mentors for the youngest, and all children learn about service and leadership throughout school life, not least in the amazing residential trips every year.
Add to this some time for project-based collaborative learning, Forest school, lots of sport and opportunities for fresh air. We want there to be emphasis on social responsibility, understanding our place in the community and our impact on the world around us.

Senior School Prospectus
Thanks for coming through to this part about our Senior School. It’s just a short overview of what we do – and what we don’t do!
KHS gives senior students the best parts of Prep school, adjusted to be appropriate for young people in the 21st century. This means continuing with small class sizes, having sensible amounts of homework, a balanced day with plenty of outdoor time and teachers who are kind and helpful, and who know you as an individual.
We don’t believe in a 11+ test, nor in regular and stressful class tests. Your teachers will monitor your progress and give you feedback on how you’re doing, and how they think you can improve. Your voice really matters, and there are many ways to (politely, of course!) make comments on the options you’re given, the balance of freedom versus support, whether the tasks you’re doing are giving you the chance to show your potential.
We have residential trips for Years 7 and 8, and then there are subject-specific trips for Years 9-11 to support your subject options. Year 11s carry the most senior roles in the school – until they have other things to focus on in the summer and the Year 10s take over. The oldest children take on Mentor roles to look after the Year 7s, ensuring that there is a positive cycle of helping and reassuring those less experienced than ourselves.
Students in the Senior school choose bespoke pathways. That means an array of options in traditional and less traditional subjects for GCSE, Cambridge National and BTEC qualifications. It means being able to get involved in DofE, or HPQ. It means all kinds of creative outlets. It means being prepared for highly academic 6th forms, or more hands-on apprenticeships and everything in between. It means being treated with respect as you approach adulthood, while never leaving you to fend for yourself.

School Houses
At Kingswood House, pupils are placed into one of our three Houses when they join the school: Rudolph, Rogers or Turing.
House points are awarded for academic effort and attainment or at a teacher’s discretion. Regular competitions are held across sports, art, music and drama, generating a lot of excitement from the participants! House points are accrued every week, and an overall winning House is rewarded with a fun day out at the end of the academic year. Each House chooses a charity to support at the start of the term for that academic year.
This year we also have a staff house, Marie Curie, so pupils can acknowledge staff in the same way and promote healthy competition between staff and pupils.

Scholarships & Bursaries
Bursaries
We believe that talent, potential and ambition are not confined by financial circumstances so we are happy to consider applications for a Bursary funded place at KHS. By offering a supported bursary place we aim to ensure that our school becomes an even more inclusive and vibrant learning environment, enriched by a broad spectrum of perspectives, backgrounds and experiences. This step aligns with our mission to ‘Believe’; fostering excellence, nurturing individuality and preparing all students to make meaningful contributions to the wider world.
Once you have registered your child with us and paid the Registration Fee – £180 (including VAT) if you are interested in applying for Bursary support please complete the relevant section on there.
Conditions of a Bursary Award
We always want to consider as many families as possible, which is why we work with a trusted third-party Bursary Administration Ltd, BAL, to ensure all financial and family circumstances assessments are fair, objective, independent and completely confidential. You can read the main conditions here.
Scholarships
Scholars at KHS are recognisable (if you look hard!) by a subtly different school tie. Scholarships do not come with strings attached – winning a music scholarship does not necessarily compel you to choose GCSE music or sing in the choir (though both these are likely to be recommended!). They are designed to acknowledge a child’s effort in achieving an unusually high competence in an area of interest or (and this or is part of what makes KHS a bit different to most schools) a real sense of potential which we want to highlight. We make no distinction, nor is there any hierarchy, in the various domains in which scholarships are won. We rate musical, sporting, creative, dramatic and academic prowess with equal awe and wonder. Far more important than a recognition of past progress, the awarding of scholarships serves as a promise by the school, to parents and pupils alike, to recognise children, to stretch, challenge and inspire them to go onto new heights. As Spiderman often observed, with great power comes responsibility. Well, strictly speaking it was his uncle Ben, and even more strictly we can see the sentiment in Voltaire, and the Gospel of St Luke and the hadiths of Mohammed and many other places.
We do our best properly to consider children at any moment for scholarships, so if you want to nominate your child then please don’t wait or think you have missed the chance. With that said, we do have organised processes to coincide with entry into Years 3, 5, 7 and 9 [aka 7+, 9+, 11+ and 13+] and this is undoubtedly the most efficient and straightforward way for all concerned. Our application deadline for this year is 6th December; I hope you’ll give it some thought.
A final thought: scholarships are not the ‘be all and end all’. They are not a short-cut to preferential treatment or the latest trendy ‘must-have’. To retain any meaning and integrity, there needs to be a process of selection, which means that not all applicants are successful. Some children have talent but aren’t ready yet to undergo the process of compiling an art portfolio, or perform in front of a judge. At KHS we believe in the boundless potential of all our pupils, irrespective of the tie they wear. Are scholarships elitist? Yes, a bit. Are they for everyone? No, probably not? On balance, and given that we can either do things, or not do them, do we believe in giving children a chance to show what they can do and get all the support they need to take their abilities to the highest level possible? Definitely, and that’s the point of this page. As always, to discuss this or any other aspect of school life, please don’t hesitate to give me or Ellie Barrett, Head of Admissions, a call.
Matthew Bryan, Headmaster

Payment of fees
Each termly invoice must be paid in full on or before the first day of term. The School reserves the right to refuse to allow a pupil to attend, and to withhold any references, while fees remain unpaid.
A full term’s notice in writing is required before the withdrawal of a pupil or the change of status, otherwise a full term’s fees will be payable. If a pupil is withdrawn from the School without such notice, or if for any reason a pupil leaves the School or is required by the School to leave during the course of the term, no fees are returnable. A term’s fees will also be payable where a parent fails to provide the required notice of withdrawal, after acceptance of a place. Cases of serious illness or genuine hardship may receive special consideration on written request.
Please see the School’s Terms & Conditions for further information about the payment of Fees and Extras. The School’s Terms & Conditions are available on request from the School Ofiice or on the website.
School fees refund scheme

If for any reason the cover is no longer required, you may cease participation in the scheme, at any time, by advising the school. Details can be obtained from the Bursar.
